Consult Summary:
- Adult patient with 3-day persistent severe headache (diffuse, worse over right eye) with photophobia and intermittent visual disturbances; partial relief with ibuprofen; no focal neurologic symptoms. Assessed as possible migraine; plan for in-person neurological and fundoscopic exam, BP check, trial of a stronger NSAID plus acetaminophen, and safety-net to emergency care if worsening.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe “blinding” headache for 3 days, constant, interfering with work and concentration.
- Onset/duration/progression: Sudden onset upon waking 3 days ago; continuous since; intensity fluctuates (reported 8/10, reduces to ~5/10 after ibuprofen but does not resolve).
- Location/character: Generalized headache, more intense over right eye; occasional stabbing pain when standing quickly; sensation of “something moving” with abrupt head movement.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia; intermittent “shooting light”/visual disturbance; mild nausea without vomiting. Denies numbness, tingling, weakness, changes in smell or taste. Sleeping well; not waking at night from pain; can wake with headache in the morning.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Worse with rapid standing and abrupt head movement; partial relief with ibuprofen.
- Prior headaches: Intermittent, short-lived (<2 days) headaches in the past that responded to ibuprofen; no prior visual symptoms, nausea, or vomiting with past episodes.
- Recent eye check: Recent optometry exam reported no change in vision.
- Infection/ENT/respiratory: Denies fever, sore throat, ear pain, sinus pain, cough, phlegm, nosebleeds, or hemoptysis.
- General: No weight change; reports low energy likely due to persistent headache.
- Function: Works from home; required partial to full days off due to headache.

Past Medical History:
- History of intermittent short-duration headaches (previously responsive to ibuprofen).
- “Pain when younger” with no cause found and resolved (details not documented).
- No other chronic medical conditions documented.

Medications:
- Combined oral contraceptive pill (exact name not documented); started ~1 year ago; no noted side effects; no prior increase in headache frequency.
- Ibuprofen as needed for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- New prescription: “Stronger NSAID similar to ibuprofen” (dose/route/frequency not documented); advised to take with food.
- Advised may take acetaminophen (paracetamol) concurrently (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Employment: Works from home; missed part/all of work days due to headache.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks approximately “three” once weekly (quantity unclear; exact units not documented).
- Recreational drugs: Denies.
- Travel: No recent foreign travel.

Family History:
- Mother with migraines, including severe episodes with vomiting.
- No other family history reported.

Physical Examination:

Investigations:
- None documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute severe headache with photophobia and intermittent visual disturbance, right periorbital predominance; first prolonged episode (3 days). Possible migraine (visual aura suspected), but persistent duration warrants exam to exclude secondary causes.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange in-person evaluation for full neurological examination and fundoscopic (optic disc) assessment.
    - Prescribe stronger NSAID alternative; take with food; may use acetaminophen concurrently.
    - Safety-net: If pain becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes in character before the appointment, go to the emergency department; may contact clinic for further advice.
    - If symptoms resolve before the visit, appointment may be canceled per clinician.
- Issue 2: Combined oral contraceptive use in context of possible migraine with visual aura.
  - Plan:
    - Check blood pressure at upcoming visit.
    - If migraine with aura is confirmed, discuss need to change contraception (current combined pill may be unsuitable).
    - Continue current pill for now until further evaluation.
- Issue 3: Work impact due to headache.
  - Plan:
    - Symptomatic management as above; reassess functional status after treatment and evaluation.

General Plan items:
- Book appointment via support team for examination and BP check.
- Monitor symptoms; seek urgent care if deterioration occurs.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals not recorded; no in-person neurological exam or fundoscopic exam performed; no specific red-flag screening documented for neck stiffness/meningismus or thunderclap onset; exact contraceptive brand not recorded; medication doses/routes/frequencies not documented.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Some audio dropouts/unclear segments and omitted personal identifiers; overall clinical content sufficient for summary but lacks detailed specifics.
